claim: At N=64 (4 layers, d_model=64, best-of-5 controls, 10-step checkpoints), accel_step forms persistently at step 90, 90 and 80 in seeds 57, 58 and 56. All three fall inside the predicted [70, 100], and in every seed the margin stays at or above the 0.1 bar at every later checkpoint. Final layer-4 accel_step R2 is 0.909/0.875/0.882 against controls 0.769/0.731/0.709 (margins 0.139/0.144/0.173; headroom-normalized 0.61/0.54/0.59). Force never beats its control: final margin is 0.05-0.08 against a bar of 0.1, after a short spike at step 10 (margin 0.152-0.158) that falls to about 0 by steps 40-70. val_mse_ratio first drops below 1 at steps 150/150/170, 60-90 steps after accel_step forms, ending at 0.45-0.48.
confidence_note: The main prediction (persistent formation step in [70, 100] in all 3 seeds) and the val_mse_ratio timing prediction (first below 1 in [130, 170], after formation) both hold in every seed. This replicates the 80-90 formation steps of f-20261012-005950-42a7 on new seeds. Two secondary numbers fall slightly outside their predicted ranges: seed 58's final R2 is 0.875 (predicted 0.88-0.91), and seed 56's control is 0.709 (predicted 0.72-0.79). Neither changes the timing result. The formation step is threshold-sensitive. At the crossing, the margin rises only about 0.01 per 10 steps, and seed 58 crosses at exactly 0.100. A bar 0.02 higher would therefore move formation by about 20 steps. Final margins are also only 0.04-0.07 above the bar, so a fixed 0.1 threshold measures timing coarsely. The cross-seed formation spread is 10 steps (80-90). The paired N=256 arm should be compared against that spread. What would change the verdict: a rerun with different probe splits or control draws that moves any seed's persistent formation step outside [70, 100], or a finding that the 0.100 crossing in seed 58 is a rounding artifact that moves its formation step to 100. 100 is still inside the range.
